options: a:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange background and black markings.,b:Round with black and yellow coloring.,c:Square with white and red coloring.
note: Temporary work zone signs use an orange background with black letters or symbols to warn drivers of construction or maintenance activities.

question: How should you pass a bicyclist safely?
options: a:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much space as possible.,b:Drive into the bicycle lane until you can pass.,c:Honk to alert the bicyclist then pass quickly.,d:Pass on the right regardless of conditions.
note: When passing a bicycle, slow down and leave as much room as possible; bicyclists are vulnerable and may swerve to avoid hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:
options: a:Stop completely, then proceed when it is safe.,b:Slow down and drive carefully through without stopping.,c:Turn either right or left because the road is blocked ahead.,d:Stop only if other vehicles are present.
note: A flashing red signal means you must come to a full stop. After stopping, proceed only when the intersection is clear.

question: Should you always drive more slowly than other traffic?
options: a:No, you can block traffic when you drive too slowly.,b:Yes, it is always safer than driving faster than other traffic.,c:Yes, it is a good defensive driving technique.
note: While you should slow for conditions, driving excessively slower than traffic can obstruct flow and be unsafe.

question: Excessive speed most often leads to what?
options: a:High-risk decision-making and increased crash risk.,b:No change in crash likelihood.,c:Improved ability to react to hazards.
note: Excessive speed is a common factor in crashes and often leads to risky decisions without saving meaningful time.

question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops in front of large trucks or buses?
options: a:Large trucks and buses travel at higher speeds than small vehicles.,b:Small vehicle drivers cannot adequately see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.,c:Large trucks and buses require longer distances to stop than smaller passenger vehicles.
note: Due to their size and weight, large vehicles need much more distance to stop and accelerate; sudden stops in front of them increase collision risk.

question: On gravel or dirt roads, your tires:
options: a:Do not have as much traction as on pavement, so you must slow down.,b:Grip the road better than on pavement.,c:Provide the same traction as on asphalt.,d:Allow you to stop more quickly.
note: Tires have reduced traction on loose surfaces; slow down and increase stopping distance to avoid skids.

question: In very heavy fog you should slow down and:
options: a:Turn your lights to their high beam setting.,b:Turn on your emergency flashers.,c:Turn your lights to their low beam setting.,d:Turn on parking lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog because high beams reflect off moisture and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer signals you to stop while a traffic light is green, you should:
options: a:Obey the officer's directions even if they conflict with the traffic signal.,b:Obey the traffic signal instead of the officer.,c:Follow the car in front of you as a guide.,d:Ignore the officer if the light is green.
note: Drivers must follow the instructions of law enforcement officers even when they contradict signs, signals, or markings.

question: When may you legally cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To turn left into a driveway or to make a permitted left turn.,b:To pass a slow-moving truck.,c:To pass another car in traffic.
note: You may not pass across double solid yellow lines except to turn left into/exit a driveway or make a permitted U-turn where allowed.

question: What happens to tire effectiveness as your speed increases on a wet roadway?
options: a:Your tires become less effective at removing water, increasing the risk of hydroplaning.,b:Water has no effect on modern tires.,c:Deep water is safer than shallow water.
note: At higher speeds on wet roads, tires may lose the ability to clear water from the road surface, increasing the chance of hydroplaning.

question: A properly adjusted seat belt should:
options: a:Be buckled snugly across your hip bones and the lower abdomen.,b:Be left loose for comfort.,c:Be hidden under your clothing.,d:Wrap around your neck.
note: Lap belts should fit snugly across the hips and lower abdomen; shoulder belts should lie across the chest, not the neck.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers reach a four-way stop at the same time, who goes first?
options: a:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:One driver may proceed without stopping.
note: When two drivers arrive simultaneously at a four-way stop, yield to the driver on your right and then proceed when safe.

question: What are the colors of signs that show distance to the next highway exit?
options: a:Green with white letters.,b:Yellow with black letters.,c:Red with white letters.,d:Blue with white letters.
note: Guide and destination signs, including exit signs, are green with white lettering or symbols.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you pass another vehicle?
options: a:If your lane is next to a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear ahead.,b:In a curve or on a hill.,c:By using the shoulder of the highway.
note: You may not pass on hills, curves, or by using the shoulder; only pass where pavement markings and sight distance allow it.

question: Which action best helps you avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Deciding before you start drinking that you will not drive.,b:Simply telling others you won't drive after drinking if offered a drink.,c:Calling a taxi only after you've been drinking.
note: The best way to avoid alcohol-related crashes is to decide before drinking that you will not drive; alcohol impairs judgment, so decisions made after drinking are less reliable.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive slower than the posted speed limit?
options: a:You see a police car.,b:You are entering a highway where there are other cars.,c:When conditions (weather, road, visibility) make driving less than perfect.,d:Only when other drivers are going slower than the limit.
note: Reduce speed below the posted limit when roads are wet or slippery, when visibility is poor, or whenever conditions make the posted limit unsafe.

question: What does a red arrow pointing right mean on a traffic signal?
options: a:You must not turn in that direction until the arrow turns green.,b:You may turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.,c:You may turn after coming to a complete stop.
note: A red arrow means stop; you must wait until a green signal or arrow allows the turn.

question: If another vehicle cuts closely in front of you, what should you do first?
options: a:Take your foot off the accelerator to increase the following distance.,b:Honk and brake hard immediately.,c:Swerve into the next lane.
note: If a vehicle cuts in, remove pressure from the accelerator to increase space rather than braking hard or swerving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.,b:Decrease your speed further.,c:Refuse to allow other cars to pass.
note: Driving significantly slower than the flow of traffic can be hazardous. On two-lane, two-way roads, if traffic is backing up, you are required to pull off the road and let other vehicles pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a driver behind you signals to pass, how should you respond?
options: a:Slow down to allow room in front of your vehicle for the pass.,b:Maintain your speed so they pass quickly.,c:Speed up to prevent the pass.
note: Slow down to create space in front of your vehicle so the other driver can pass more easily and safely.

question: How can you prevent drowsiness on a long trip?
options: a:Stop at regular intervals for rest and stretching.,b:Turning up the car radio.,c:Slowing down while continuing to drive.
note: Schedule regular stops to rest and stretch; this is more effective than radio or slowing down to prevent drowsiness.

question: If you become tired while driving, what is the best action?
options: a:Stop to rest or switch drivers.,b:Drink coffee and continue driving.,c:Open a window and keep driving.
note: If you feel drowsy, stop in a safe place to rest or switch drivers—driving while tired slows reactions and increases crash risk.

question: When driving in fog, you should use your low beam headlights:
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only on highways,d:Only when the fog is dense
note: Low beam headlights reduce glare that high beams produce in fog, improving visibility. Use low beams in foggy conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view at an intersection is blocked, what's the correct approach?
options: a:Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.,b:Maintain your speed and look both ways.,c:Slow down and look both ways.
note: Stop and creep forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions before entering the intersection.

question: Which of these does NOT occur after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.,b:Your judgement of speed and distance is distorted.,c:You are less alert.,d:None of the above.
note: Alcohol impairs reaction time, judgment, and alertness. All listed effects occur after drinking; none are exceptions.

question: If you're angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Take a few minutes to calm down before getting behind the wheel.,b:Drive on the interstate to cool off.,c:Play loud music to avoid thinking about the argument.
note: Strong emotions impair driving ability; give yourself time to calm down before operating a vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady yellow traffic light at an intersection indicates you should:
options: a:Slow down and prepare to stop.,b:Go.,c:Yield to other cars.,d:Speed up to beat the red.
note: A steady yellow means that a red light will follow soon. Slow down and prepare to stop unless you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely.

question: Which types of drugs can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Certain allergy medicines,b:Marijuana,c:Cold remedies,d:All of the above
note: Many medicines — prescription and over-the-counter — as well as illegal drugs and other substances, can impair driving. Read labels and avoid driving if affected.

question: If you have a tire blowout, which steps are recommended?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas, do not immediately apply the brakes, and gradually slow to a stop.,b:Apply the brakes immediately and firmly.,c:Keep accelerating to reach a safe area.
note: On a blowout, release the accelerator, avoid hard braking, slow down gradually, then steer to a safe spot and stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or false: When approaching a stop sign that has no marked crosswalk, drivers must stop before entering the intersection.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only if a crosswalk exists.,d:Only at night.
note: At a stop sign you must stop at the stop line or, if none, before entering the crosswalk or the intersection.

question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, drivers should use:
options: a:Parking lights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Low beam headlights.,d:Interior dome lights.
note: Low beam headlights help others see your vehicle in poor weather. High beams can create glare and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Toward the right (into the curb).,b:Toward the left.,c:Keep them straight ahead.
note: When parked facing downhill, turn the wheels toward the curb so if the vehicle rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

question: How can you keep track of traffic behind you?
options: a:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b:Turn and look out your back window.,c:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.
note: Regularly check your rearview mirror to be aware of traffic approaching from behind.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal turns green, you should:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and any traffic still in the intersection.,b:Accelerate as quickly as possible to clear the intersection.,c:Back up slowly to allow others to move.,d:Ignore pedestrian crossings until the light cycles again.
note: A green light means you may go, but you must first yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim its high beams at night, what is the safest action?
options: a:Look ahead toward the left edge of your lane.,b:Look straight ahead in your lane.,c:Look ahead toward the right edge of your lane.
note: Avoid staring at the oncoming headlights; look toward the right edge of your lane and use peripheral vision to monitor the road.

question: What should you avoid doing when driving through a construction zone?
options: a:Slowing down to stare at the scene (rubbernecking).,b:Passing with extra caution.,c:Following the posted detour signs.
note: Do not slow down to look at incidents or workers; rubbernecking both causes congestion and increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should not pass in which situations?
options: a:When school bus lights are flashing.,b:When approaching an intersection.,c:All of the above.,d:On a hill or curve.
note: Do not pass near intersections, on hills or curves, before/at railroad crossings, or when a stopped school bus is displaying flashing red lights.

question: When parallel parking, your vehicle should be no farther than what distance from the curb?
options: a:14 inches.,b:10 inches.,c:Six inches.,d:18 inches.
note: Your vehicle should be no farther than 18 inches from the curb when parallel parked.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with flashing signals, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and look for a train; remain at least 15 feet from the nearest rail if warning devices are active.,b:Slow down and look for a train but continue if nothing is visible.,c:Speed up to clear the crossing quickly.
note: If a railroad signal is giving warning, stop no closer than 15 feet from the rails and wait until it is safe to cross.

question: Must you yield the right-of-way to a disabled pedestrian using a cane, guide dog, or other device?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Pedestrians with assistive devices have the same rights as other pedestrians and must be yielded to.

question: What is the correct method for backing a vehicle safely?
options: a:Turn your head and look through the rear window while backing.,b:Rely solely on your mirrors and sensors.,c:Open your door to look behind you.
note: When backing, always look over your shoulder through the rear window—don’t depend only on mirrors or sensors; small objects and children can be hard to see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are you required to signal every time you pull away from a curb?
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only when other vehicles are nearby.,d:Only during daytime.
note: You must use the proper turn signal any time you pull away from a curb to inform other road users of your intentions.

question: If your vehicle starts to hydroplane, what should you do?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly to prevent sliding.,b:Slow down gradually and avoid applying the brakes.,c:Drive at a constant speed to gain traction.,d:Turn sharply to regain control.
note: If hydroplaning occurs, ease off the accelerator and let the vehicle slow; do not brake hard or make sudden steering moves.

question: Before backing out of a driveway when children are nearby, you should:
options: a:Get out of the vehicle and walk to the rear to be sure the way is clear.,b:Sound your horn so the children will hear you.,c:Rev the engine to warn the children.,d:Back up slowly while looking only in your mirrors.
note: When children are near, always exit and check behind the vehicle rather than relying only on mirrors; make sure the path is clear before backing.

question: At night, which is the hardest to see?
options: a:Pedestrians.,b:Road signs.,c:Other motorists.,d:Streetlights.
note: Pedestrians are generally the hardest to see at night compared to signs or other roadway objects; use caution and reduce speed.

question: When should you slow down while exiting a highway?
options: a:After you have moved into the exit lane.,b:On the main road just before the exit lane.,c:Only when you see a toll booth.
note: Get into the exit lane well in advance and then reduce speed after entering that lane, not on the main traveling lane.

question: A pedestrian begins crossing in front of your vehicle. What should you do?
options: a:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.,b:Flash your lights.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: Slow and be prepared to stop whenever pedestrians are crossing; always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in crosswalks.

question: Is it lawful to drive alongside a motorcycle in the same lane?
options: a:False — you must not share a lane with a motorcycle.,b:True — it is allowed if both fit.
note: Motorcyclists need the full lane width to maneuver safely; never attempt to share a lane with them.

question: If you are about to be struck from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Letting go of the steering wheel.,b:Pressing your head firmly against the head restraint.,c:Applying your brakes if safe to do so.
note: Do not let go of the steering wheel; brace against the seat back and head restraint and be ready to apply brakes to avoid being pushed into another vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, where should you glance?
options: a:Over your left shoulder.,b:Your right side mirror.,c:At the rearview mirror.
note: Glance over the shoulder in the direction you plan to move to see areas not visible in your mirrors.

question: A curb painted which color indicates only short parking stops are permitted?
options: a:White.,b:Blue.,c:Yellow.
note: White painted curbs indicate that only short stops (e.g., passenger drop-off) are permitted.

question: To cross a railroad track safely you should:
options: a:Listen and look both ways for trains, and only proceed when it is safe.,b:Look both ways only when warning lights are flashing.,c:Cross quickly if a train is approaching.,d:Never stop if no gate is present.
note: Always look and listen for approaching trains from both directions and obey any warnings before crossing tracks.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
options: a:Do not pass from your lane.,b:Slow down and prepare to stop.,c:Pass with caution when safe.
note: A solid yellow line adjacent to your lane indicates passing is prohibited from your direction.

question: Drivers who eat or drink while driving tend to:
options: a:Have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicles.,b:Make no driving errors.,c:Drive more carefully because they are alert.,d:Be exempt from distracted driving laws.
note: Eating, drinking, or similar distractions take hands and eyes off driving tasks and increase the risk of lane departures and crashes.

question: Which of the following helps prevent crashes by informing others of your intentions?
options: a:Communicate with other road users by signaling and using horn when needed.,b:Ignore other drivers.,c:Drive only on side streets and avoid main roads.
note: Communicate by signaling, using emergency lights, or the horn when necessary so others know your intentions and avoid unexpected actions.

question: What does a green arrow signal displayed for a turn mean?
options: a:Traffic in the indicated lane may proceed to turn in the direction shown; it has the same authority as a circular green for that movement.,b:It only applies on one-way streets.,c:You may proceed only if accompanied by a circular green light.
note: A green arrow gives a protected turn movement; traffic in the indicated lane may turn in the direction of the arrow while it is displayed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you make a right turn on red?
options: a:After coming to a complete stop and if no sign prohibits it and it is safe.,b:Before coming to a complete stop.,c:If pedestrians have not yet crossed the crosswalk.
note: You may turn right on a solid red after a full stop if the turn is permitted and safe; yield to pedestrians and other traffic.

question: Which action most commonly blocks smooth traffic flow?
options: a:Slowing down to look at a collision scene.,b:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,c:Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.,d:Driving at the posted speed limit.
note: Rubbernecking at crash scenes causes slowdowns and congestion. Keep moving at a safe speed and avoid distractions.

question: How should you check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Using the inside rearview mirror.,b:Using both inside and outside rearview mirrors.,c:Turning your head to look over your shoulder.
note: Always turn your head to check blind spots before each lane change; mirrors alone may not reveal vehicles in blind spots.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Turn off the ignition carefully to stop the engine, apply brakes, and move off the road.,b:Slam on the brakes immediately.,c:Blow your horn continuously.
note: If the accelerator sticks, shift to neutral if needed, turn off the ignition carefully to stop the engine without locking steering, brake, and pull off to safety.

question: Why is night driving more hazardous?
options: a:Because distance and speed are harder to judge in the dark.,b:Because the speed limit increases at night.,c:Because there are fewer cars on the road at night.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it difficult to judge distance and the speed of other vehicles; you can only see as far as your headlights illuminate.

question: Is it ever permissible to drive around lowered gates at a railroad crossing?
options: a:If no train is visible.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:When the lights have stopped flashing.,d:When the train has passed.
note: You must stop at railroad crossings when warning signals are active. Do not attempt to drive around lowered gates, even if you think no train is present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach a traffic signal that is not operating, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection (treat as all-way stop).,b:Proceed without stopping if the way is clear.,c:Drive quickly through to avoid congestion.,d:Only stop if a police officer is present.
note: Treat a nonworking traffic signal as an all-way stop: stop, then look and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.

question: How can you avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Quickly turn your head to check the blind spot in the direction you plan to move.,b:Adjust the rearview mirror frequently.,c:Honk right before changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, glance over your shoulder toward the lane you want to enter to check blind spots; don't rely solely on mirrors.

question: Which substances can impair your driving and possibly result in a DUII?
options: a:Beer, wine, and other liquor.,b:Controlled substances such as illegal drugs or some prescription medicines.,c:Inhalants such as glue or paint.,d:All of the above.
note: Alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medicines (prescription and over-the-counter) can impair driving and lead to arrest for impaired driving.

question: What message is displayed on a red, octagonal sign?
options: a:Stop.,b:One-way.,c:Do not enter.
note: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means 'STOP'—you must come to a complete stop at this sign.

question: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights and siren, what should you do?
options: a:Continue through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.,b:Stop immediately in the intersection and remain there.,c:Pull to the left and stop in the intersection.
note: If you are in the intersection, clear it by continuing through, then pull to the right and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What are the requirements for interstate driving?
options: a:Have the ability to safely drive at increased speeds.,b:Be constantly alert.,c:Both of the above.
note: Interstate driving requires both the ability to handle higher speeds safely and constant alertness to traffic conditions.

question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only if the pedestrians first wave to the driver.,b:Only if the pedestrians are not texting while walking.,c:At all times.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in crosswalks at all times, stopping when necessary to allow them to cross.

question: When should you allow a larger space cushion than usual when stopped?
options: a:When stopped on an incline (uphill).,b:At a stop sign regardless of slope.,c:When in the center lane of a multi-lane road.
note: Allow extra space when stopped on an uphill slope so the vehicle in front can move without rolling back into you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When leaving an interstate via an exit ramp, when should you reduce speed?
options: a:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,b:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.,c:As you approach the deceleration lane.
note: Maintain highway speed until you enter the deceleration lane, then slow to the exit ramp's advisory speed.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, how should you proceed?
options: a:Prepare to yield to any train and do not cross until you can clear the tracks completely.,b:Always stop before crossing the tracks regardless of conditions.,c:Cross the tracks immediately and quickly.
note: At crossings without signals, be prepared to yield and never cross unless there is room on the far side for your entire vehicle.

question: Changing lanes should be done:
options: a:Gradually and carefully.,b:Quickly and often to keep traffic moving.,c:Only when other vehicles are in your blind spot.,d:Without signaling if the lane is clear.
note: Make lane changes smoothly, signal in advance, check mirrors and blind spots, and execute only when safe.

question: Is it safe to stop on railroad tracks if moving with a stream of vehicles?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Never stop, stand, or park on railroad tracks. Only cross if there is room for your entire vehicle on the other side.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct procedure when changing lanes?
options: a:Check the side mirror and glance over your shoulder to ensure the lane is clear.,b:Check only the inside rearview mirror.,c:Slow down dramatically before moving.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors and glance over your shoulder toward the lane you intend to enter to verify it is clear.

question: How is 'distracted driving' best defined?
options: a:Any activity that takes your attention away from driving.,b:Something that usually improves driving performance.,c:Only activities that involve using a phone.
note: Distracted driving includes anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving tasks and is a major contributor to collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must drivers yield?
options: a:Pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Oncoming traffic.,c:Other drivers who are already in the intersection.
note: When turning left you must yield to oncoming traffic; also yield to pedestrians and others already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While waiting in an intersection to complete a left turn, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels straight while waiting.,b:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.,c:Flash your headlights to warn drivers.
note: Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left so a rear-end collision won't push you into oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you make room for vehicles entering the freeway?
options: a:Merge into another lane if possible or slow to create a gap.,b:Maintain your speed and position.,c:Always speed up to prevent merging.
note: If possible, move over to make room for entering vehicles; if not, adjust your speed to allow them to merge safely.

question: When making a left turn, must you yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction?
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only if the bicyclist is in a bike lane.,d:Only at night.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming bicyclists in the same manner as you would yield to other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's turn signals are not working, what should you use to indicate a turn?
options: a:Hand signals.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Sound your horn.
note: If turn signals fail, use standard hand signals to show your intention to turn or stop until the signals are repaired.

question: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you must stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Firmly pump your brakes to maintain steering control.,b:Hold down the brake pedal continuously.,c:Lightly tap the brakes.
note: For vehicles without ABS, pumping the brakes helps avoid wheel lock and allows you to steer while stopping.

question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, what are they signaling?
options: a:Turn left.,b:Turn right.,c:Come to a stop.,d:Slow down.
note: A left arm extended upward indicates the driver intends to turn right. Observe and adjust your driving accordingly.

question: When crossing a sidewalk from a driveway or alley, what should a driver do?
options: a:Expect pedestrians to yield the right-of-way.,b:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk area.,c:Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
note: When leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot, you must stop before driving onto a sidewalk area because pedestrians and traffic have the right-of-way.

question: Pentagonal (five-sided) signs are used to indicate:
options: a:School zones and school crossings.,b:No passing zones.,c:Speed limits.,d:Construction zones.
note: A pentagonal sign warns that you are entering a school zone or crossing area; be alert for children.

question: If an emergency vehicle with lights approaches while you are on a one-way street, what must you do?
options: a:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,b:Drive with your flashers on and continue.,c:Speed up and exit the street.
note: On a one-way street, when approached by an emergency vehicle using lights or siren, drive toward the nearest roadside and stop to allow it to pass.

question: If you are following a school bus or a tank truck, what precaution should you take at railroad crossings?
options: a:Be prepared to stop at all railroad crossings.,b:Pass them on the right.,c:Decrease your following distance so you can get around them quickly.
note: School buses and tank trucks carrying flammable liquids must stop at railroad crossings; be prepared to stop when following them.

question: Which is a common sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:They are weaving between lanes.,b:They are making quick and sudden stops.,c:They are driving more slowly than the normal traffic flow.
note: Drunk drivers may weave between lanes, make erratic movements, drive too slowly, or make quick sudden stops.

question: A solid yellow X shown above a reversible lane means:
options: a:The lane signal is about to change to a red X; clear the lane.,b:You may drive normally in this lane.,c:The signal is about to change to a green arrow.,d:The lane is open only for turning.
note: A steady yellow X warns drivers that the lane is about to close (red X); you should move out of that lane as soon as safely possible.

question: How does smoking while driving affect driving?
options: a:Helps maintain driver alertness.,b:Is a distracting activity.,c:Does not affect driving abilities.
note: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving can distract you by causing you to take hands off the wheel or eyes off the road.

question: Which statement about roadwork zones is true?
options: a:You must Slow for the Cone Zone and obey work zone signs and reduced speeds.,b:Fines are always the same as under normal conditions.,c:You only need to slow if workers are visible.,d:Passing is always allowed at full speed.
note: Reduce speed, obey signs, and be prepared to stop in work zones; slowing improves safety for workers and drivers.

question: An octagonal (8-sided) traffic sign always indicates what?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A speed advisory.,c:A hospital.
note: An eight-sided sign is always a stop sign; you must come to a complete stop when approaching one.

question: If you constantly pass slower vehicles on a two-lane road, what is likely to happen?
options: a:Get you to your destination much more quickly and safely.,b:Increase your chances of a collision.,c:Help prevent traffic congestion.,d:Improve fuel efficiency.
note: Frequent passing increases risk of collisions. Avoid unnecessary passing on two-lane roads.

question: If you stop on the roadside at night, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Turn on your emergency flashers and leave low-beam headlights on.,b:Turn off all lights to conserve battery.,c:Use parking lights only.
note: When stopped at night, use your emergency flashers and keep low-beam headlights on so other road users can see your vehicle.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Reaction time and coordination.,b:Alertness and concentration.,c:All of the above.
note: Alcohol and drugs impair alertness, concentration, reaction time, and coordination—all critical driving skills.

question: What is a likely symptom of a failing vehicle suspension?
options: a:Problems controlling the vehicle or excessive bouncing.,b:Loud squealing brakes.,c:Play (slack) in the steering wheel.
note: A worn suspension can make the vehicle hard to control and may cause excessive bouncing after bumps; suspension problems affect handling and safety.

question: How quickly does the average body process alcohol?
options: a:One alcoholic drink an hour.,b:Two alcoholic drinks an hour.,c:Three alcoholic drinks an hour.
note: On average, the body metabolizes about one standard alcoholic drink per hour, though many factors affect impairment.

question: What will help a person overcome the effects of alcohol?
options: a:Only the passage of time.,b:Drinking coffee.,c:Fresh air and exercise.
note: Nothing speeds sobering up other than time; coffee, fresh air, or other measures do not reduce blood alcohol content.

question: Which driving technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Engage the vehicle’s four-wheel drive.,b:Get off the highways as quickly as possible.,c:Reduce your speed and increase following distance.
note: On snow or ice, reduce speed and increase following distance; avoid quick stops and turns to prevent skids.

question: At a railroad crossing, which of the following should you watch for?
options: a:Vehicles that must stop at all crossings (school buses, hazardous material trucks) and multiple trains.,b:Only one train at a time.,c:Only school buses.
note: Approach railroad crossings cautiously and be aware that some vehicles must always stop, and more than one train may be approaching.

question: When a traffic signal shows a steady green arrow, drivers:
options: a:May turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Must stop and wait for a solid green light.,c:Can only go straight through the intersection.,d:Have no right to turn in the arrow direction.
note: A green arrow indicates a protected turn in that direction, but you must still yield to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.

question: Why must you be cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.,b:Bicycles always have the right-of-way.,c:You are always moving slower than the bicycle.,d:Bicyclists must yield to all vehicles.
note: A bicyclist may need to swerve to avoid hazards; an oncoming vehicle may not expect you to pull out to pass, so take extra care.

question: As you enter a roundabout, whom should you yield to?
options: a:Pedestrians and bicyclists crossing, and traffic already in the roundabout.,b:Only the vehicles in the roundabout.,c:Only pedestrians at the entrance.
note: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing and to any traffic already circulating in the roundabout.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs tell drivers?
options: a:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed to be driven.,b:Potential or suggested driving speeds for the area.,c:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic.,d:The speed you must always drive regardless of conditions.
note: Speed limit signs indicate the maximum (or sometimes minimum) legal speed under ideal conditions. You must slow down when conditions require it.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign typically indicates:
options: a:Yield.,b:Warning.,c:Stop.,d:Regulatory sign.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are used to warn drivers about special conditions or hazards ahead, often in yellow or orange.

question: In traffic moving at 50–55 mph, how can you reduce accident likelihood?
options: a:Stay within that speed range and flow with other traffic.,b:Drive a few miles per hour faster than others.,c:Drive a few miles per hour slower than others.
note: Traveling at about the same speed as the surrounding traffic (within posted limits) reduces conflicts and accident risk.

question: Collisions are more likely to happen when:
options: a:One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.,b:All vehicles travel at the same speed.,c:One lane of traffic is going in the same direction.,d:Traffic lights always work.
note: Vehicles moving significantly faster or slower than surrounding traffic increase the risk of collisions.

question: A center line that is a broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Permitted from the side next to the solid yellow line.,b:Not permitted from either direction.,c:Permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.,d:Only allowed during daylight hours.
note: When the center has a broken line next to a solid line, passing is allowed from the side with the broken line and prohibited from the side with the solid line.

question: You are about to turn right and a pedestrian with a guide dog is at the corner ready to cross. You should:
options: a:Wait until the person has crossed before making your turn.,b:Tell the pedestrian when to cross.,c:Turn off your engine until they finish crossing.,d:Pass in front of them slowly.
note: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes must always be given the right-of-way; wait until they have crossed safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it safe to move back into the right lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When you are one vehicle length ahead.,c:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: Return to the driving lane only after you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror and it's safe to do so.

question: Any amount of alcohol in a driver's blood can affect what?
options: a:Judgment and physical coordination.,b:Right-of-way privileges.,c:Knowledge only.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol can impair judgment and coordination; impairment can occur below the legal BAC limit.

question: A pedestrian began crossing after the 'Don't Walk' started flashing and is in the road when your light turns green. What should you do?
options: a:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.,b:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,c:Wait until the pedestrian has finished crossing before proceeding.,d:Honk to make them hurry.
note: At a green light you must yield to people already in the intersection. Wait until the pedestrian has cleared the roadway before moving.

question: When you need to change lanes, what steps are important?
options: a:Check your blind spot.,b:Make sure the lane is clear before entering.,c:Signal your intentions ahead of the lane change.
note: Always signal sufficiently before changing lanes, check your blind spot, and ensure the target lane is clear before moving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right.,b:The driver on the left.,c:Whoever signals first.
note: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.

question: What can happen to a bicyclist who disobeys traffic laws?
options: a:They are in the right because bicyclists don’t have to obey traffic laws.,b:Can be ticketed.,c:Will always receive a warning from law enforcement.
note: Bicyclists have the same duties and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers and can be ticketed for violations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive at the posted maximum speed limit?
options: a:Under ideal conditions.,b:During the day.,c:During the night.
note: The posted maximum speed is the legal limit under ideal conditions; adjust speed lower for poor weather or visibility.

question: After several beers, the only way to reduce the effects of alcohol is:
options: a:Taking a cold shower.,b:Waiting several hours.,c:Drinking several cups of coffee.,d:Exercising vigorously.
note: Time is the only reliable method for alcohol to leave the body. Coffee, cold showers, or exercise do not speed alcohol elimination.

question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings you should always:
options: a:Look to the sides of your vehicle to check for approaching traffic and pedestrians.,b:Stop, listen, and proceed cautiously always.,c:Slowly pass vehicles stopped for no reason.
note: Whenever people may cross or where lines of traffic meet, look left and right to ensure the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at the same time at a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,b:One driver may continue without stopping.,c:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
note: At a four-way stop where two vehicles arrive simultaneously, yield to the driver on your right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach a yield sign, what is your responsibility?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to close enough cross traffic that would cause a conflict.,b:Only yield to vehicles on your right.,c:Slow down but never stop under any circumstances.
note: At a yield sign you must give right-of-way to traffic already in the lane or intersection you intend to enter; be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: True or false: Drivers are not required to yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk.
options: a:False,b:True,c:Only at marked crosswalks.,d:Only when children present.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked and certain unmarked crosswalks. The statement that drivers are not required to yield is false.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do with the brakes?
options: a:Avoid braking; stay off the brakes and steer to regain control.,b:Brake abruptly to stop the skid.,c:Pump the brakes rapidly at high speed.
note: If you start to skid, do not slam on the brakes; ease off the accelerator and steer smoothly to regain traction.

question: When driving in bad weather, what should drivers do about following distance?
options: a:Increase their following distance.,b:Decrease their following distance.,c:Maintain the same distance as in dry conditions.,d:Tailgate the vehicle ahead to control traffic.
note: In poor weather, increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead to allow more time to stop or react.

question: At a crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:You must yield to pedestrians.,b:Pedestrians must yield to you.,c:Construction workers must yield to you.
note: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks (marked or unmarked), and drivers must yield unless traffic control signals indicate otherwise.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, how should you proceed?
options: a:Assume the driver may open a door and use extra caution.,b:Speed up to pass quickly.,c:Slam on your brakes if a door opens.
note: Approach parked vehicles cautiously and be ready for doors opening or pedestrians stepping into the roadway.

question: When near a blind pedestrian using a cane or guide dog, how should you drive?
options: a:Proceed normally.,b:Take the right-of-way.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: Slow, yield, and be prepared to stop to avoid endangering a blind or visually impaired pedestrian.

question: Which statement is correct about changing lanes?
options: a:Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and over your left shoulder for a left lane change in addition to using mirrors.,b:You only need to look in your mirrors.,c:Vehicles with two outside mirrors have no blind spots.
note: Always check mirrors and glance over the appropriate shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes.

question: How is distracted driving best described?
options: a:Behavior that is extremely risky and takes attention from driving.,b:Something that rarely happens.,c:Generally safe if brief.
note: Distracted driving is extremely risky behavior that removes attention from driving tasks and increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following has the highest authority and must be obeyed over the others?
options: a:A police officer directing traffic.,b:A steady red traffic light.,c:A stop sign.
note: Directions from authorized traffic officers (police, fire police, highway work area flaggers, school crossing persons) take precedence over signs, signals, and pavement markings.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Human error.,b:New drivers.,c:Bad weather.
note: Most crashes occur because drivers make errors such as not seeing another vehicle or reacting incorrectly to traffic situations.

question: If a child appears about to run into the street, you should:
options: a:Sound a sharp blast on your horn as a warning.,b:Start to prepare to slow down only.,c:Flash your headlights repeatedly.,d:Speed up to pass before the child moves.
note: If a pedestrian, especially a child, is about to enter the roadway in front of you, sound a sharp blast of your horn to warn them and take any safe evasive action.

question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, what must drivers do?
options: a:Stop, regardless of your direction of travel.,b:Stop only if you are driving in the same direction.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: When a school bus is loading or unloading children with flashing red lights, all directions of traffic must stop.

question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of the road indicate?
options: a:Passing is permitted when it is safe.,b:A construction zone is ahead.,c:Passing is prohibited from both directions.
note: Broken yellow lines separate two-way traffic and allow passing if no oncoming traffic is present and it is safe.

question: May only vehicles with special plates or placards for persons with disabilities park in spaces reserved for them?
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only if the driver has a permit displayed.,d:Only on weekends.
note: Reserved accessible parking spaces may only be used by vehicles displaying Persons with Disabilities plates, Disabled Veteran plates, or valid disabled placards.

question: Which behavior is part of defensive driving?
options: a:Keep your eyes moving to look for hazards.,b:Put one car length between you and the car ahead.,c:Look only at the car directly in front of you.
note: Defensive driving means scanning ahead and around for potential hazards rather than staring at the road directly in front of your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, you should return to your lane when:
options: a:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,c:You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.,d:You hear the other driver honk.
note: Only move back into the travel lane when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror, indicating a safe gap.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is correct?
options: a:Even over-the-counter and prescription drugs can impair your driving.,b:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,c:Any prescription drug is safe if you don't feel drowsy.
note: Prescription and over-the-counter medications can impair driving ability; it's illegal to drive under the influence of any drug that adversely affects your ability to drive safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing another vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Check your mirrors and blind spots and signal before changing lanes.,b:Honk repeatedly to warn the other driver.,c:Re-enter the lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
note: Ensure the passing lane is clear by checking mirrors and blind spots, signal your intention, and only return when it is safe and you can see the passed vehicle in your mirror.

question: Which of the following about driving speed is true?
options: a:As your speed increases, the chance of a fatality increases.,b:As your speed increases, so should your following distance.,c:Both of the above.,d:Speed does not affect stopping distance.
note: Higher speeds increase crash severity and require greater following distance because stopping distances grow with speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the proper lane, you should:
options: a:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.,b:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.,c:Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.,d:Make a U-turn at the intersection instead.
note: Never make last-minute turns; continue to the next intersection and make the turn from the correct lane safely.

question: What does a single broken yellow center line indicate on a two-lane road?
options: a:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when it is safe.,b:Passing is prohibited in both directions.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and passing is prohibited.
note: A single dashed yellow line separates opposing traffic and indicates passing is permitted when it can be done safely.

question: True or false: Pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections always have the right-of-way.
options: a:False,b:True,c:Only at marked crosswalks.,d:Only at signalized intersections.
note: Pedestrians have the right-of-way in many situations, but the statement 'always' is not accurate. Yield when necessary and be alert near crosswalks and intersections.

question: If your wheels slip off the edge of the pavement while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Continue with wheels off the pavement, slow down, then steer back when safe.,b:Jerk the steering wheel to force back onto the pavement.,c:Slam on your brakes and stop immediately.
note: If your wheels leave the pavement, ease off the gas, gently apply brakes to slow, and when safe steer gradually back onto the road—do not make abrupt steering motions.

question: Which of the following is true regarding railroad crossings?
options: a:You must stop when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal.,b:You always have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing.,c:You should speed across if no train is visible.,d:You never need to stop for a crossing without lights.
note: Stop at railroad crossings when directed by signs, a flagger, or active warning devices; always exercise caution near tracks.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers.
note: Use low beams in fog, rain, or snow because high beams can reflect and reduce visibility.

question: Wearing both the lap belt and the shoulder belt in a two-part system increases protection. True or False?
options: a:True,b:False
note: If your vehicle has both a lap and shoulder belt, you should wear both; wearing only one part reduces protection in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are already in an intersection when the light turns yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Increase your speed so as not to cause an accident.,b:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.,c:Stop immediately.
note: If you are already in the intersection when the signal turns yellow, clear it as quickly and safely as possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you begin a left turn when turning from a one-way street onto a one-way street?
options: a:The lane closest to the left curb.,b:Any lane so long as it looks safe.,c:The center lane.
note: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, start the turn from the lane nearest the left curb.

question: Before changing lanes, which check should you perform?
options: a:Check your side view mirror.,b:Quickly turn your head to check for other vehicles.,c:Check your rearview mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, check both side and rearview mirrors for approaching traffic and, just before moving, glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When facing a green light with pedestrians in the intersection, you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,b:Proceed because you have the right-of-way.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection.,d:Ignore pedestrians in the crosswalk.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians and any vehicles already in the intersection, including when turning on a green light.

question: Which of these does stopping distance NOT depend on?
options: a:Your own reaction time.,b:The time of day.,c:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.
note: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, vehicle weight, brake and tire conditions, road conditions, visibility, and speed—not the time of day.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only if a crossing guard is present.,b:Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.,c:At all times.
note: Pedestrians who use guide dogs or white canes (with or without a red tip) must be given the right-of-way at all times.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using lights or a siren, what must you do?
options: a:Pull to the right curb or side of the road and stop.,b:Slow down and keep moving in your lane.,c:Keep driving in your lane until it passes.
note: You must promptly pull over to the right and stop to give way to emergency vehicles using lights or sirens.

question: If the driver ahead is distracted (one-handed and talking to a passenger), you should:
options: a:Flash your lights to warn them.,b:Give the vehicle extra space.,c:Avoid following the driver's example.,d:Know the driver is reducing their safety margin by being inattentive.
note: Distracted drivers are a higher risk of sudden errors; increase the following distance and be prepared for unexpected moves.

question: When parallel parking facing downhill, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your front wheels toward the curb or side of the road.,b:Turn your wheels away from the curb.,c:Keep wheels straight ahead.
note: When parking downhill, turn the wheels toward the curb or edge of the road so the vehicle will roll into the curb if it moves.

question: Are drivers always required to stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: On a two-lane road, drivers in both directions must stop for a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended stop arm.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it acceptable to drive on the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:No, never under normal circumstances.,b:Yes, if the shoulder is wide enough.,c:Yes, if the vehicle ahead is turning left.
note: Never pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder; other drivers may unexpectedly re-enter the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When doing so would interfere with traffic or be unsafe.,b:When turning left into a driveway.,c:When the car ahead is disabled.
note: You may cross a broken line to pass or change lanes only if it is safe and will not interfere with other traffic.

question: What do round traffic signs typically warn drivers about?
options: a:An upcoming railroad crossing.,b:School zones.,c:No passing zones.
note: Round signs are used to warn drivers of an approaching railroad crossing area; exercise extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it important to always use your turn signal?
options: a:Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.,b:Changing lanes.,c:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,d:All of the above.
note: Use signals to communicate your intentions whenever changing lanes, entering traffic, or moving into or out of parking spaces.

question: Lack of sleep affects driving ability similarly to which substance?
options: a:Alcohol.,b:Amphetamines.,c:Anger.
note: Fatigue impairs driving in ways similar to alcohol—for example, being awake 18 hours can impair driving about as much as a 0.05% BAC.

question: Which statement about backing your vehicle is true?
options: a:Backing is always dangerous because rear visibility is limited.,b:Backing is safe if you drive slowly.,c:Backing is only dangerous for large vehicles.,d:Backing is never dangerous with mirrors.
note: Backing is risky due to limited rear visibility; use caution, helpers, or exit the vehicle to check when necessary.

question: How are reversible lanes usually marked?
options: a:Double dashed yellow lines.,b:Single solid white lines.,c:Single dashed white lines.,d:Double solid red lines.
note: Lanes that change direction during the day are typically marked by double dashed yellow lines and controlled by lane-use signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive much slower than the speed limit and create a backup of traffic, you should:
options: a:Is a very safe driver.,b:Always has the right-of-way.,c:Must pull off the road and let other vehicles pass.,d:Should not let following cars pass.
note: Driving significantly below the flow of traffic can be hazardous; if you are blocking traffic on a two-lane road you may be required to pull off and let others pass.

question: When must you obey instructions from school crossing guards?
options: a:At all times.,b:Only during school hours.,c:Unless you do not see any children present.,d:Only when police are present.
note: Drivers must always obey crossing guards' directions when they are present to protect pedestrian safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After you pass another vehicle traveling the same direction, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:About three seconds after passing.,c:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
note: Return to the lane only after you can see the passed vehicle's entire front in your rearview mirror and it is safe to do so.

question: If your wheels run off the pavement edge, what is the recommended recovery?
options: a:Turn back onto the roadway immediately.,b:Reduce speed, check traffic, and gradually re-enter the roadway when it is safe.,c:Stop where you are and call for help.,d:Accelerate to regain control.
note: Do not jerk the steering wheel to return to the road. Slow down, check traffic, and carefully steer back onto the pavement when it is safe.

question: Why is following a motorcycle too closely dangerous?
options: a:Because a motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.,b:Because motorcycles do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.,c:Because motorcycles brake more slowly than cars.,d:Because motorcycles always have the right-of-way.
note: Motorcycles can stop quickly; following too closely reduces your ability to avoid a collision if they brake suddenly.

question: True or false: How fast you drive does not affect the distance your vehicle travels after you apply the brakes.
options: a:Only in wet conditions.,b:False,c:It depends on the vehicle's weight.,d:True
note: As speed increases, stopping distance increases. Faster speeds require more distance to stop safely.

question: When approaching a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and wait until the stop arm is withdrawn.,b:Honk your horn before passing.,c:Drive past the bus if no children are visible.,d:Pass slowly on the left.
note: If a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the signals end and the arm is retracted.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the statewide speed limit in school zones (unless otherwise posted)?
options: a:15 mph.,b:10 mph.,c:25 mph.,d:20 mph.
note: The default school zone speed limit statewide is 15 miles per hour unless signs indicate another limit.

question: How can you ensure your physical condition won't impair driving?
options: a:Keep physically fit and have regular physical exams.,b:Drive within your physical limitations.,c:Know the effect of any medicine on your driving ability.
note: Monitor your medical fitness to drive: know medication effects, stay within your limits, and get regular checkups to remain safe.

question: If you must drive in foggy conditions, you should:
options: a:Use your low beam headlights.,b:Turn on your hazard lights and drive fast.,c:Use your high beams to see farther ahead.,d:Drive at the posted speed limit regardless of visibility.
note: Use low beams in fog; high beams reflect off fog and worsen visibility. Use low beams and reduce speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic ahead is blocking an intersection you should:
options: a:Wait to enter the intersection until you can clear it completely.,b:Enter the intersection if the light is green to avoid blocking others.,c:Honk to make the traffic move forward.,d:Pull alongside the vehicle in front of you.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it without stopping; avoid blocking cross traffic when lights change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Whenever it helps prevent collisions.,b:Often, even at controlled intersections.,c:Never; it confuses other drivers.,d:Only at uncontrolled intersections.
note: Never assume other drivers will yield. Give up the legal right-of-way when it will prevent a crash.

question: When a school bus on your side of the road has red lights flashing, you must:
options: a:Stop until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,b:Slow to 10 mph and pass carefully.,c:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,d:Proceed if no children are visible.
note: When a school bus displays flashing red lights and extends its stop arm, you must stop until the signals end and the arm is retracted.

question: Where are a truck's blind spots typically located?
options: a:On the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the truck.,b:Directly behind the body only.,c:On the immediate left of the cab only.
note: Large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger vehicles; drivers cannot see cars behind or beside them if those vehicles are in the truck's blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to turn left at an intersection with a green light but heavy oncoming traffic, what may you do?
options: a:Enter the intersection and wait for a safe gap to complete your left turn.,b:Immediately back out of the intersection.,c:Turn from any lane available.,d:Ignore oncoming traffic and make the turn.
note: On a green light you may move into the intersection to prepare for a left turn, then complete the turn when oncoming traffic clears and it is safe.

question: Hydroplaning is most often caused by:
options: a:Driving too fast for wet conditions.,b:Excessive stops.,c:Sudden turns.
note: Hydroplaning typically occurs when tires cannot clear water at higher speeds, causing loss of road contact.

question: How should you check a blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look over your shoulder toward the lane you will enter.,b:Use only the inside rearview mirror.,c:Use only the side mirror.
note: Even with properly adjusted mirrors, some areas (blind spots) are not visible. Turn your head and glance over your shoulder to check them before changing lanes.

question: Is it lawful to drive through, around, or under railroad crossing gates or barriers?
options: a:False — you must never drive through or under railroad gates.,b:True — you may if no train is visible.
note: It is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive through, around, or under gates or barriers at railroad crossings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the maximum speed limit on a rural interstate highway?
options: a:75 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:40 mph.
note: On rural interstate highways, the default maximum speed limit is 75 mph unless a different limit is posted.

question: When backing up your vehicle you should:
options: a:Look through the rear window.,b:Press hard on the gas pedal.,c:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,d:Use only your side mirrors.
note: When reversing, turn and look through the rear window. Mirrors do not show the entire area directly behind your vehicle.

question: What does a flashing red traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:The same thing as a stop sign — stop completely and proceed when safe.,b:The light is about to turn green.,c:You do not have to come to a complete stop.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop and yielding to traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

question: What effect does even a small amount of alcohol have on driving skills?
options: a:Even small amounts reduce concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.,b:Only amounts above the legal limit have any effect.,c:Alcohol improves driving ability.
note: Any amount of alcohol can impair mental functions needed for safe driving; no one can safely drink and drive.

question: After a minor intersection crash with no injuries and little damage, what should you do with your vehicle?
options: a:If possible, move the vehicle out of the traffic lane.,b:Leave the vehicle where it is until law enforcement arrives.,c:Never move the vehicle for any reason.
note: If no one is injured and it's safe, move the vehicle out of traffic to prevent further collisions and to reduce congestion.

question: Is it legal to pass across double solid yellow center lines? True or False?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate no passing in either direction; do not cross them to pass another vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You come to an intersection showing a flashing red light. You should:
options: a:Come to a full stop, then proceed only when it is safe.,b:Slow and proceed if clear.,c:Stop only if other cars are approaching.,d:Ignore it if no cross traffic is present.
note: A flashing red light means stop — treat it like a stop sign and proceed when the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, how should you proceed?
options: a:Slow or stop if needed and yield to cross traffic close enough to be a hazard.,b:Always come to a complete stop regardless of traffic.,c:Yield only to vehicles coming from your right.
note: At a yield sign, slow or stop if necessary and yield the right-of-way to traffic or pedestrians close enough to cause conflict.

question: When making an emergency roadside stop, is it necessary to use the parking brake?
options: a:False — you should set your parking brake.,b:True — you do not need to set the parking brake.
note: When stopped for an emergency, set your parking brake and turn on emergency flashers to alert other drivers.

question: A flashing yellow X above a reversible lane indicates:
options: a:The lane may be used only to complete a left turn.,b:The signal is about to change to a red X.,c:Drivers may use this lane to travel normally.,d:The lane is open for merging.
note: A flashing yellow X means the lane is only for left turns; you may enter it only to make a left turn.

question: How does increasing your vehicle’s speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:Decreases your field of vision.,b:Makes it easier to see cross traffic.,c:Increases your field of vision.
note: As speed increases, your field of vision narrows; you must be extra alert for potential hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver merging onto an interstate from an entrance ramp should:
options: a:Yield to drivers already on the interstate.,b:Force other cars to make room for them.,c:Always have the right-of-way.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp before merging.
note: Vehicles entering the interstate must yield to traffic already on the highway and merge only when it is safe to do so.

question: At an intersection, what does a flashing red light require you to do?
options: a:Stop completely, then proceed when safe — same as a stop sign.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:You do not have to stop if the way is clear.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop; yield to traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct practice for slowing on a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Wait to slow down until you are actually on the exit ramp.,b:Brake hard before entering the ramp.,c:Keep your speed constant once on the ramp.
note: Do not slow abruptly on the mainline; wait until you have moved onto the exit ramp before reducing speed to the ramp advisory speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, whom should you yield to?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.,b:Yield to the vehicle on your left.,c:Wait until there are no vehicles present before proceeding.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, drivers should yield to vehicles on their right when arriving simultaneously.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a Merging traffic sign on the freeway, you should:
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles; move over a lane if it is safe to do so.,b:Always remain at your present speed regardless of merging traffic.,c:Speed up to prevent congestion.,d:Honk at the entering driver.
note: If you are in a multi-lane roadway and it is safe, move over or adjust speed to allow entering vehicles to merge safely.

question: How can you help the driver behind you keep a safe following distance?
options: a:Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,b:Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.,c:Maintaining a steady speed.,d:Frequently tapping your brakes to signal them.
note: Maintaining a steady speed and signaling early for maneuvers helps the driver behind keep a safe space and reduces sudden braking.

question: What is the effect of slowing down just to look at collisions or unusual events?
options: a:It causes additional traffic congestion.,b:It prevents rear-end collisions.,c:It improves traffic flow.
note: Slowing to look at an incident creates traffic backups and increases the chance of secondary crashes; keep moving safely past the scene.

question: A leaking exhaust system can:
options: a:Make you drowsy while driving.,b:Cause your car to use more oil.,c:Increase engine power.,d:Improve fuel efficiency.
note: Fumes from a leaky exhaust can be toxic and may cause drowsiness, unconsciousness, or death in a short time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Only where road signs and pavement markings indicate passing is permitted and it is safe to do so.,b:Within an intersection if you see no oncoming vehicles.,c:On a curve if you have a clear view ahead.
note: You may pass only where signs and markings allow and where there is enough space and visibility to pass safely; never pass in intersections or on curves with limited sight distance.

question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning?
options: a:Keep your tires properly maintained.,b:Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.,c:Watch out for standing water or puddles.,d:Use cruise control to maintain traction.
note: Reduce speed on wet roads and avoid cruise control when conditions are slippery. Proper tire maintenance also helps, but slowing is key.

question: Which action helps reduce incidents of road rage?
options: a:Talk on your cell phone while driving.,b:Use your horn frequently.,c:Always signal your intention when changing lanes.
note: To help prevent road rage, obey traffic laws, signs, signals, and pavement markings and always signal before lane changes.

question: When following a motorcycle, you should:
options: a:Allow extra space if you are behind a passenger vehicle.,b:Allow extra space when following a station wagon.,c:Allow extra space in front of your vehicle when following a motorcycle.,d:Follow at the same distance as you would any other car.
note: Motorcycles can stop more quickly and are harder to see. Give them extra space so you can stop safely if needed.

question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:On all sides of your vehicle — front, sides, and rear.,b:Only in front of your vehicle.,c:Only behind your vehicle.
note: Maintain space on all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards and avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a conflict.,b:Yield only to vehicles on your right.,c:Always slow down and proceed without stopping.
note: At a yield sign, slow or stop if necessary and yield to traffic or pedestrians that are near enough to create a hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever permissible to drive off the road to pass another vehicle?
options: a:No — you may not drive off the paved portion or onto the shoulder to pass.,b:Yes — if the vehicle ahead is turning left.,c:Yes — if there are two or more lanes going your direction.
note: Never pass another vehicle by driving off the paved or main-traveled portion of the road onto the shoulder.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the maximum speed in a business or residential area?
options: a:30 mph.,b:20 mph.,c:45 mph.,d:35 mph.
note: The default maximum speed in business and residential districts is 30 miles per hour unless signs indicate a different speed.

question: What is true about bicyclists and traffic laws?
options: a:They are exempt from traffic laws.,b:They have the same rights and duties as motor vehicle drivers and can be ticketed.,c:They always receive a warning instead of a citation.
note: Bicyclists must obey the same traffic laws as motorists and can be cited for violations.

question: A broken yellow centerline means:
options: a:Passing on the left is allowed when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is never permitted in either direction.,c:You must stay in your lane at all times.,d:You may pass on the right only.
note: A broken yellow line means you may cross to pass if it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic; a solid line restricts passing.

question: If you are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane, you should:
options: a:Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for vehicles in your blind spot before changing lanes.,b:Only check your mirrors and change lanes quickly.,c:Signal and move without checking blind spots.,d:Sound your horn, then change lanes.
note: Check mirrors, signal, and look over the shoulder toward the lane you intend to enter to check the blind spot before changing lanes.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, you should:
options: a:Press down on the brake pedal as hard as you can.,b:Slow down gradually and do not brake abruptly.,c:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.,d:Turn off the ignition immediately.
note: Grip the wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and allow your vehicle to slow before gently braking and pulling over when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which action should you never take?
options: a:Change lanes while within an intersection.,b:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: Never change lanes within an intersection; always check mirrors and blind spots before moving.

question: When parking facing uphill on a street with a curb, you should:
options: a:Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.,b:Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.,c:Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.,d:Leave your wheels straight.
note: To prevent rolling into traffic when parked uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels sharply away from the curb. If there is no curb, turn toward the edge of the road.

question: Why should you use headlights in rain, snow, or fog?
options: a:To keep your engine warm.,b:So others can see your vehicle.,c:To warn others of bad weather conditions.,d:To improve your radio reception.
note: When visibility is reduced by weather, headlights make your vehicle easier for others to see. If wipers are needed, low beams must be on.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:
options: a:Remain calm and move out of their way rather than retaliating.,b:Flash your lights to show them they are wrong.,c:Immediately pursue and confront the driver.,d:Block them from changing lanes.
